requirement:
Conversion preserves history rather than performing a new review. It invokes
no model and needs no model configuration. It reconstructs no missing historical
dependencies from current sources and assigns no current procedure identity
to records lacking one. Missing historical metadata is explicitly identified
as legacy information.
rationale:
The two marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.provenance`. I did not read the `record` helper in `src/authoring/sdk.rs`, which the SDK test uses to build the old record. The assertions on its output (`review_version` is `*`, and `view(new)` equals `old`) show that it produces a legacy record.

- **Preserves history, not a new review.** `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` runs over four subject kinds: requirement, example, citation and site. For each one it asserts that `record.output == old` and that the rationale is still "Historical rationale.". It also asserts that `view(&native) == old` after `encode`. The SDK test `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` checks the same on the file path: `view(new) == old` after `author_evidence_with_options`.
- **Invokes no model and needs no model configuration.** The SDK test calls `author_evidence_with_options` with the nonexistent configuration name `missing-configuration` and `EvidenceOutput::File`. It expects success with `result.is_none()` and a rewritten file, so conversion needs no model configuration and runs no review. A conversion that tried to resolve or call a model would fail here.
- **Reconstructs no missing historical dependencies from current sources.** The format test uses historical inputs that point at `deleted.rs`/`fn[old]` and at text that no longer exists. It asserts that `record.dependencies[0]` equals the dependency built from the old input's selector and fingerprint. It asserts exactly 3 dependencies for a definition (two inputs plus the references digest) and exactly 2 for the other subject kinds. Re-resolving against current sources, or adding dependencies, would change those values. After decoding the native form again, it asserts the dependencies are unchanged. It also asserts that no "source text" appears in the native output.
- **Assigns no current procedure identity.** The format test asserts `record.version == None`. It asserts the converted native record has `review_version == "*"` and `format_version == 1`. The SDK test asserts `review_version == "*"` after conversion with current sources. A current review version would fail both assertions.
- **Missing metadata identified as legacy.** The `*` `review_version` marker in the converted record is asserted in both tests. `view` round-trips back to the original legacy record.

I found no uncovered input class or scenario in the subject's text. The partial-header and invalid-record tests belong to other requirements. No acknowledgments are needed.

text: :::{req} evidence_conversion.provenance
Conversion preserves history rather than performing a new review. It invokes
no model and needs no model configuration. It reconstructs no missing historical
dependencies from current sources and assigns no current procedure identity
to records lacking one. Missing historical metadata is explicitly identified
as legacy information.
:::{req} evidence_conversion
Habeas Codicem supports in-place conversion of legacy evidence to the versioned
representation under {cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, preserving
the historical values of its judgments, rationales, recorded inputs, and all
review-specific fields.
:::{req} evidence_conversion.atomic
A write-capable conversion atomically replaces the selected file at its existing
location. Readers observe either the original complete record or the converted
complete record. Failure before replacement leaves the original file unchanged.
:::{req} evidence_conversion.idempotent
Converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.
:::{req} evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness
When Habeas loads legacy evidence with an unknown criterion version, the SDK
record holds `None`. In-place conversion writes `"*"` in `review_version` so
the converted file preserves that history. An unknown version passes the
version check under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.version_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.
For new assessments, Habeas Codicem's validation value supplies a concrete review version
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
:::{req} evidence_conversion.provenance
Conversion preserves history rather than performing a new review. It invokes
no model and needs no model configuration. It reconstructs no missing historical
dependencies from current sources and assigns no current procedure identity
to records lacking one. Missing historical metadata is explicitly identified
as legacy information.
:::{req} evidence_conversion.writes
Conversion writes only through a write-capable migration or authoring path.
Loading for `load_evidence`, CI, status inspection, or book rendering leaves
evidence files unchanged. Authoring with `--stdout` performs no in-place
conversion and creates or changes no evidence files or directories under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.persistence`.
